title: fix: do not flush Redis after a failed cron push
body:
## Bug and impact The weekly cron update could wipe Redis user-agent ranking data even when the generated commit never reached `master`. That permanently loses a week of traffic counters and leaves the published lists stale until enough new data accumulates. ## Root cause In `.github/workflows/cron.yml`, the update job ran `git push origin ${{ github.head_ref }} || true`. On `schedule` / `workflow_dispatch`, `github.head_ref` is empty, and `|| true` masked any push failure. The `flush` job only requires `update` to succeed, so Redis was deleted afterward regardless of whether the push landed. ## Fix - Push with an explicit refspec: `git push origin HEAD:master` - Remove `|| true` so a failed push fails the update job, skips flush, and skips the healthcheck success ping ## Validation - Confirmed from a successful cron log that the rendered command was `git push origin || true` (empty head_ref) - Confirmed `flush` is gated only by `needs: [update]` - Workflow YAML change reviewed for bash `-e` behavior: push failure now aborts before healthcheck and before flush
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > CI workflow-only change that reduces operational risk by tightening push failure handling before Redis flush. > > **Overview** > Fixes a weekly cron bug where **Redis could be flushed even when the user-agent update never landed on `master`**. > > The update job now pushes with **`git push origin HEAD:master`** instead of **`github.head_ref`** (empty on scheduled runs). **`|| true` is removed** so a failed push fails the job, which blocks the dependent **`flush`** step and the success healthcheck ping. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 74306d4317cb62b1f4475b5d1ac058cf2cdbf0c0. title: fix: refuse to publish short user-agent lists
body:
## Bug and impact The weekly update pipeline could overwrite the published top-100 user-agent lists with an empty or short array if Redis had little or no data at update time (for example after `flush` + a `workflow_dispatch` re-run, or a sparse Redis dataset). That change would be committed, pushed to `master`, and released to npm, breaking consumers that assume a populated list. ## Root cause `bin/util.js` filtered bots and sliced to `n` without checking that enough non-bot agents remained. `bin/update.js` then wrote whatever it got to `src/*.json` with no minimum-size guard. ## Fix - Add `selectTopUserAgents()` that throws when fewer than `n` non-bot user agents are available, so the update job fails instead of publishing bad data. - Add tests for the short-list rejection path and for keeping the published lists at 100 entries. ## Validation - `npm test` (lint + ava) — all 5 tests passed.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Small, defensive change to the update helper with unit tests; no auth or runtime consumer API changes beyond failing fast when data is insufficient. > > **Overview** > The weekly update path could commit and ship **empty or undersized** top-100 user-agent JSON when Redis was sparse or flushed, because bot filtering and slicing never enforced a minimum count. > > **`selectTopUserAgents()`** in `bin/util.js` now keeps the top `n` non-bot agents and **throws** if fewer than `n` remain, so `top()` (used by `bin/update.js`) fails the job instead of writing bad `src/*.json`. **`isBot`** and **`selectTopUserAgents`** are exported for tests. > > Tests assert published lists stay at **100** entries and cover success, partial data, and empty input for the new guard. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 333e09d684e2103cc9bb0175d8fac305a5bd59ef. Bumps [ava](https://github.com/avajs/ava) from 7.0.0 to 8.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from ava's releases.

v8.0.0

Breaking Changes

AVA now expects Node.js 22.20, 24.12 or newer.

Internally AVA is now fully ESM. This is possible now that Node.js supports loading ES modules using require() calls and simplifies AVA's types and internals.

If you use AVA from a CommonJS project you'll have to update your imports:

-const test = require('ava');
+const {default: test} = require('ava');

We expect an increasing number of projects to be ESM only. As per the above, CommonJS is still supported, but we don't expect cjs extensions to be used. The default file extensions are now js and mjs. Specify extensions: ['cjs', 'js', 'mjs'] for AVA to run test files with the cjs extension.

All test files (and those loaded through AVA's require config) are now loaded via import(). Use customization hooks for transpilation. The object form of the extensions configuration is no longer supported.

If you use AVA with @​ava/typescript you must upgrade that package to v7.

New Features

There's two new test modifiers courtesy of @​sindresorhus: test.skipIf() to skip a test based on a runtime condition. test.runIf() is the inverse: the test only runs when the condition is true.

test.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')('not on Windows', t => {
	t.pass();
});

test.runIf(process.platform === 'linux')('Linux only', t => {
t.pass();
});

These work with other modifiers like .serial and .failing:

test.serial.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')('serial, not on Windows', t => {
	t.pass();
});

test.failing.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32')('expected failure, not on Windows', t => {
t.fail();
});

Other Changes

  • TAP reporter is more defensive when restoring the original error name, thanks to @​ninper00 in avajs/ava#3415

The current source of top user agents, [techblog.willhouse.com](https://techblog.willshouse.com), has been down since the start of December 2023. It returns a "ERROR 404 - PAGE NOT FOUND" message whenever I try to access it. This website has been unstable for a long time and I doubt it will be fixed anytime soon.

I suggest changing the source of top user agents to a more reliable and up-to-date website, such as [Useragents.me](https://www.useragents.me/). This website provides a self-updating list of the latest and most common user agents for all device types, operating systems, and browsers. It also has an API that can be used to get the user agent data in JSON or TSV format.

This change would improve the quality and accuracy of the top user agents data and make the project more useful for web scrapers, developers, and researchers.

Adding Node.js version file support

In scope of this release we add the node-version-file input and update actions/cache dependency to the latest version.

Adding Node.js version file support

The new input (node-version-file) provides functionality to specify the path to the file containing Node.js's version with such behaviour:

  • If the file does not exist the action will throw an error.
  • If you specify both node-version and node-version-file inputs, the action will use value from the node-version input and throw the following warning: Both node-version and node-version-file inputs are specified, only node-version will be used.
